question_text: Find the derivative of the function Tan⁻¹(log x).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what goes into the 1 + u² and what the inner derivative is.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply the Tan⁻¹ rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. The u in 1 + u² is the whole inside function, log x, so the denominator is 1 + (log x)². It is not 1 + x².
steps.memory_tip: Whatever sits inside Tan⁻¹ is squared and added to 1. Copy the inside part exactly, then square it.
lines: Let y = Tan⁻¹(log x), where log is the natural logarithm and x > 0.
Take u = log x. Then d/dx(Tan⁻¹u) = 1/(1 + u²) · du/dx

recall.must_convey: That d/dx(Tan⁻¹u) = 1/(1 + u²)·du/dx with u = log x, so the denominator is 1 + (log x)².
accept: tan inverse u gives one over one plus u squared times du by dx
the denominator is one plus log x whole squared
u is log x so square log x not x
lopala unnadi log x, adi square cheyyali
one over one plus log x squared to start

steps.why: Substituting the inside function into 1 + u² is the whole method mark. Writing 1 + x² is the standard slip and gives the derivative of a different function.
common_mistakes: Writing the denominator as 1 + x² instead of 1 + (log x)².
Writing 1 + log x² , which squares x rather than log x.

steps.label: Differentiate log x and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. d/dx(log x) = 1/x, so an x joins the denominator. Both factors go under the line together.
steps.memory_tip: A log inside always produces a factor 1/x, so the final denominator carries an x as well as the bracket.

accept: log x differentiates to one by x
the answer is one over x into one plus log x whole squared

log x ki one by x, kaabatti x kinda vasthundi
multiply by one over x at the end

steps.why: The 1/x is the second mark on its own. Without it the expression is the derivative with respect to log x, not with respect to x.
common_mistakes: Putting the x in the numerator instead of the denominator.

insider_note: The Tan⁻¹ rule squares its argument, so the denominator is 1 + (log x)² and not 1 + log(x²). The inner derivative then contributes the 1/x.
